clue.text: Action to be taken about the French gun handed over

indicators.note: the action word is to be wrapped around the next pieces, as if taken round them

parts.note: a deed is an action
le is the French masculine word for 'the'
gat is old American slang for a gun

explanation.surface: Orders given about a French firearm being surrendered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be taken about' puts LE and GAT inside DEED.
explanation.definitionFit: To delegate a task is to pass it on to someone else, so a delegated job has been passed across.

clue.text: Specialist making small change in exercise

indicators.note: the coin is placed inside the word for exercise

parts.note: to exercise power is to exert it
p, a penny, is the smallest British coin

explanation.surface: A coach tweaks one small detail of a workout routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts P (penny) inside EXERT; 'exercise' is a verb here, as in exercising authority.
explanation.definitionFit: An expert is a person with specialised skill or knowledge.

clue.text: With monstrous head and sickening cry and ears like wings" Chesterton (The Donkey)

definitions.text: With monstrous head and sickening cry and ears like wings" Chesterton (The Donkey)

parts.words: With monstrous head and sickening cry and ears like wings" Chesterton (The Donkey)
parts.note: a quotation from G. K. Chesterton's poem The Donkey with one word missing before 'wings'; the solver supplies the poet's adjective

explanation.surface: A line of verse describing a donkey's ugly head, braying cry and great flapping ears.
explanation.walkthrough: The poem's line runs 'And ears like ___ wings': the missing word means wandering, straying.
explanation.definitionFit: The poet compares the donkey's ears to wandering, roving wings, the adjective meaning straying from a course.

clue.text: Song setting a conservationist body on edge

parts.note: NT is the National Trust, the British charity that conserves historic houses and land
a hem is the finished edge of cloth

explanation.surface: Something is making a nature charity nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on edge' reads as nervous, but 'on' only places HEM after A and NT.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthem is a rousing song, often a national or church one.

clue.text: Getting in range possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals these letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone is coming within reach, perhaps of a target.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges the letters of IN RANGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Earning money is getting it in return for work.

clue.text: Keen for action?

parts.note: keen is read as the noun, a wailing cry, and the cry is one raised as troops go into a fight

explanation.surface: Someone eager to get stuck in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' looks like the adjective eager; it is the noun for a loud wail, here a shout before fighting.
explanation.definitionFit: A shout raised by soldiers charging into combat is a wail, or cry, made for the fighting.

clue.text: The underworld, being on the level, scoffed-so incongruous

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld and a name for the underworld itself
par means equal, on the level
to scoff food is to eat it greedily, so scoffed means ate

explanation.surface: Hell, honesty and greedy eating make a strange combination.
explanation.definitionFit: Disparate things are so unlike one another that they do not fit together.

clue.text: A reckless guy's road speed varied greatly

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: the letters are changed a great deal, so they are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tearaway driver keeps changing speed wildly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'varied greatly' rearranges ROAD SPEED.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a bold, lawless outlaw who takes wild risks.

clue.text: Bringing a hundred into line is quite easy

indicators.note: with 'Bringing', says the next pieces go inside the word for line

parts.note: a file is a line of people one behind another
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Getting a hundred people to queue up is no trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bringing ... into' puts A and C inside FILE.
explanation.definitionFit: Facile describes something achieved without effort, often too simply.

clue.text: Musical high-spots for the workers

parts.note: an opera is a musical drama
tors are rocky hilltops, high points in a landscape

explanation.surface: The best moments of a show are laid on for the staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Operators are people who work machines or run a business.

clue.text: Close or street with not a single dog

parts.note: not a single one is none, the figure zero, shaped like O
a pup is a young dog

explanation.surface: A cul-de-sac or road with no dogs at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' looks like a street name like the neighbouring 'street'; it is the verb to block.
explanation.definitionFit: To block a hole or pipe is to seal it shut.

clue.text: Translation of "The Butterfly" making a poet grin

indicators.note: making says the poet's grin is worked into something new, a rearrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A poet smiles while rendering a work called The Butterfly into another language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Translation of' is a link: rearranging the butterfly's name 'makes' A POET GRIN, as the clue claims, so 'making' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The orange-tip is a common European butterfly whose males have orange wing tips.

clue.text: Blunder by trusted leader causing great consternation

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a blunder is an error

explanation.surface: A trusted chief makes a mistake that alarms everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Terror is extreme fear, a stronger form of alarm.

clue.text: Compass acknowledgments of debt, and that's enterprising

parts.note: compass in the sense of range or scope is ambit
IOUs are signed notes saying I owe you

explanation.surface: Covering many debts is a bold business move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compass' is not the direction-finder but scope, extent.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambitious person is driven and full of enterprise.

clue.text: Mostly in deep water

explanation.surface: Someone is largely out of their depth.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means for the most part, and literally out at sea, the main being an old word for the open ocean.

clue.text: Moving after professional encouragement

indicators.note: the moving piece comes after the professional one

parts.note: pro is short for professional
moving, as a noun, is motion

explanation.surface: A move comes after a coach's urging.
explanation.definitionFit: Promotion is active furthering or advancing of a cause or product.

clue.text: An article for example backing seniority

parts.note: a, the indefinite article

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the abbreviation is read right to left

parts.note: eg is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: Support for a grammar example about rank by length of service.
explanation.definitionFit: Seniority is being older or longer in place, which comes with years.

clue.text: A record height

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing vinyl record

explanation.surface: A best-ever altitude.
explanation.definitionFit: An Alp is a high mountain, one of the peaks of the Alps.

clue.text: Some rather feeble weak-willed sheepish creature

indicators.note: some of the words, a part of them, holds the answer

explanation.surface: A timid, spineless person is shown as lamb-like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' picks out the letters running across 'feeblE WEak'.
explanation.definitionFit: A female sheep is literally a sheep-like animal; 'sheepish' is used in its literal sense.

clue.text: The collier needs a pound to get drink

definitions.note: the page runs the two words a drink together, and the definition is the drink

parts.note: a collier is a coal miner
L is the abbreviation for pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A coal worker wants a pound so he can buy something to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Mineral is British for a fizzy soft drink, short for mineral water.

clue.text: Crushed to produce fine stuff

explanation.surface: Something squashed to make good material.
explanation.definitionFit: Worsted means defeated soundly, and is also a smooth fine woollen cloth.

clue.text: Food-mixed type

explanation.surface: A bit of a jumble of food.
explanation.definitionFit: A pie is a baked dish, and in printing pie is jumbled loose type.

clue.text: Not punctilious in previous work

parts.note: ex means former, previous
an act is a piece of work, a deed

explanation.surface: Careless in an earlier job.
explanation.definitionFit: Inexact means lacking precision, the opposite of scrupulously careful.

clue.text: Fashionable buzz as last of wine is being put down

parts.note: in means fashionable
a hum is a buzzing sound

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A trendy glow as the bottle's last drop is set down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put down' looks like setting a glass down; it means to lay in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To inhume is to bury, to lay a body in the earth.

clue.text: A carrier of young

explanation.surface: Something that carries babies.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a couch carried on poles, the other the brood born to an animal at one time.

clue.text: Taking one in sordid surroundings is excusable

indicators.note: taking means holding within, so the number goes inside the corrupt word

parts.note: venal means corrupt, open to bribery, so sordid
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Accepting a guest in squalid surroundings can be forgiven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking' puts I inside VENAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A venial sin is a minor, pardonable one.

clue.text: Border revolutionary arming

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Rebels arming themselves at the frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' rearranges ARMING.
explanation.definitionFit: A margin is an edge or border, as round a page.

clue.text: A male vied for representation in years gone by

indicators.note: presenting the letters in a new form, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man competed to be elected in olden times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for representation' rearranges A MALE VIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Mediaeval describes the Middle Ages, a long-past era.

clue.text: Anyone living in a house requires a certain amount of curtain material

indicators.note: only part of the words is taken, so the answer lies within them

explanation.surface: Every householder needs some fabric for curtains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a certain amount of' picks the letters across 'curtaIN MATErial'.
explanation.definitionFit: An inmate is one who lives in an institution or shares a house.

clue.text: Some crest! Some bird!

parts.note: some means a part
a crest is the ridge or top of a hill

explanation.surface: Admiring cries at a hilltop and a fine bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some bird!' is an exclamation of admiration; 'Some' there is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The partridge is a plump game bird.

clue.text: Concert's acceptable-no bad thing, looking back

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay

parts.note: U means upper-class, socially acceptable

indicators.note: looking back means the pair of pieces is read in reverse

parts.note: a sin is a bad deed

explanation.surface: A concert is fine, nothing wrong with it, in hindsight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looking back' turns NO SIN round into NIS ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Unison is agreement, acting in concert together.

clue.text: Setting out about fifty would be most surprising

indicators.note: the setting-out word goes about, around, the numeral

parts.note: setting out on a journey is starting
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Departing at around fifty would be a shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts L inside STARTING.
explanation.definitionFit: Startling means alarming or amazing, causing a jolt of surprise.
